text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.9% today after oil prices and refinery dynamics shifted in its favor over the past few days. Crude prices have climbed sharply—Brent hit $116 last week amid escalating Middle East tensions and Iran-related geopolitical risk—though today's news of Saudi-Iran de-escalation talks briefly pulled prices lower. The company benefits from this volatile environment: U.S. refineries are running at 93.4% capacity (historically tight), and oil inventories remain relatively low at 695 million barrels, meaning refiners can push product margins higher when crude swings create spreads between input costs and fuel prices.

The stock's broader two-week gain of 2.56% reflects the sustained elevation in crude prices—now trading above $100—which generally widens refiner profit margins if those higher oil costs don't immediately flow through to gasoline and diesel prices. Even with today's modest de-escalation move, the geopolitical premium built into crude over the past week remains in place, supporting the economic tailwinds for refiners like Marathon Petroleum.
